title: Behold a Prehistoric Lizard Tail Trapped in Amber - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontologyBehold a Prehistoric Lizard Tail Trapped in AmberProof the defense tactic has been used for at least 99 million yearsDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CDT on October 29, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIf you’ve got an escape trick that works, stick with it: A lizard tail trapped in amber reveals that these reptiles were using the same evasion tactic—lose the tail, regrow it later—almost 100 million years ago.Many species of modern lizard will detach their own tails if they get grabbed by a bird, snake, or other predator. The tail can keep wriggling as a distraction once it's been shed, allowing the lizard to make a clean getaway—with a replacement tail eventually growing back.Now, researchers have found a discarded tail in a block of amber that dates back 98.8 million years, to the time of the Late Cretaceous when dinosaurs roamed the Earth. The piece of amber analyzed by researchers measures just 18 millimeters (0.7 inches) across, so we’re talking fingertip size. The artifact has been in the Steinhardt Museum of Natural History in Israel since 2022, but has only just been described in a newly published study.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
